text:
Nina: hey team 0 I'd like to standardize a compact set of incident comms templates we use for everything: status page, customer email, quick support replies, and the short internal handoff ping. The goal: scannable, single-sentence impact at top, explicit 'what we're doing now', and a 'how to verify' line for customers.

incident-bot: New incident thread created: #20260316-03 (active). Bridge: https://redwood.internal/bridges/20260316-03 :warning:

Sam (oncall): +1. Attached a working draft below. I modeled it after last week's outage but shortened copy. Please critique.

```
STATUS PAGE TEMPLATE (one-paragraph / high-scan)
Severity: [SEV1 | SEV2 | SEV3]
Impact (one sentence): [e.g. "Customers in eu-west may see failed requests and 5xx errors when calling /v1/generate."]
Scope: [services/endpoints, regions, estimated percent affected]
Current status: [Investigating / Mitigation in progress / Monitoring / Resolved]
What we're doing now: - [action A] - [action B]
Workaround: [steps or "none"]
How to verify: [e.g. "confirm requests return 200s and tokens consumed as normal"]
Next update: [ETA or "on resolution"]
Contact: [link to bridge and incident slack thread]
```

Rae (Support): love the "how to verify" line. For support replies we need 2 canned lengths: a one-line alert we can paste into a ticket, and a slightly longer paragraph for customers who need more context. Examples below.

```
SUPPORT SNIPPET (one-liner)
We're aware of degraded [generation/embeddings] affecting some requests in [region]. We're investigating; see status page [link]. If you're blocked, please reply with org id and an example request id.

SUPPORT PARAGRAPH (customer-facing)
Hi [Customer],
We identified an issue starting at [time UTC] that may cause [symptom]. Our engineers are working on mitigation and have implemented [short action]. You can monitor progress at [status page link]. If your workflows are critical, reply with: org id, affected endpoints, and a short description and we'll escalate.
```

Liam (Product): tone guidance: start with empathy, be concise, avoid internal jargon (no "K8s pod drift" or "cache invalidation" for customers). Also add a standard sentence for "we will provide an RCA" but only after it's been validated: e.g., "We will provide a follow-up with findings and mitigations after investigation." Do not use the phrase "root cause" in early updates.

Sam (oncall): here's an enterprise outreach template (short). Please ensure it includes an explicit contact who is handling the customer's outreach.

```
ENTERPRISE OUTREACH (short)
Subject: [Service] incident affecting [Customer Name] starting [time UTC]

Hi [Name],
We27re investigating an incident that may impact your use of [service]. Symptom: [brief]. Current status: [Mitigating / Monitoring / Resolved].
Actions taken: - [action summary]
Contact for your account: [Name and email / phone].
Next update: [ETA or "on resolution"].
Sincerely,
Redwood Incident Response
```

Nina: add a required placeholder: "External comms owner: [name]" and ensure we do not promise an ETA to fix. Only promise next update time.

oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: auto-fill status page template after incident severity is set. Please ensure "External comms owner" tag is included.

Rae (Support): we should pre-write quick symptom-specific lines to save minutes. I can make a mapping: generation timeout, increased latency, 5xx error spike, auth failures. Each will have short and long variants. Example for 5xx spike: "We're seeing increased 5xx errors on [endpoint]. Retry after a few seconds. If errors persist include your request id."

Sam (oncall): adding an internal-only short ping template for handoffs and for escalations. Keep it bulletized so next on-call can pick up quickly. Make it a hard requirement from the bot.

```
INTERNAL HANDOFF (internal-only)
[Handoff start timestamp] - Handoff from [name] to [name]
Summary (1 line): [condensed impact statement]
Severity: [SEV]
Current status & actions in-flight: - [list]
Hypothesis / tests running: - [list]
Outstanding blockers & needs: - [list]
Owner for next 2 hours: [name]
Customer comms owner: [name]
Key links: [bridge | dashboards | runbook | status page]
```

Liam (Product): include an explicit "customer-facing lines already sent" block so we can avoid duplicate outreach. Also include a short "sales/AM notify" stub for enterprise customers.

Nina: propose a short 'forbidden phrases' list we inject to PRs and the bot to prevent accidental wording. Examples: "we found the root cause", "this will be fixed by X", "this is isolated to our infra" (unless verified). Also avoid internal acronyms and use plain english.

Sam (oncall): automation note: oncall-bot should pre-populate templates with severity, detected time, bridge link, and a placeholder for external comms owner. Then ping the assigned comms owner to confirm before publishing.

incident-bot: Action recorded: Template update request created (#incident-comms-20260316).

Rae (Support): quick suggestion for verification steps to add to templates: - wait 2-3 mins and retry - clear client-side cache - include sample curl command customers can run to validate service health. 

Nina: good. Add a small curl example under "how to verify":
```
curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
Expect: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

Liam (Product): append a short post-incident customer follow-up template (RCA summary) but labelled "Post-incident (RCA)". Keep it factual, include timeline, impact, mitigations, and steps taken to prevent recurrence. Also include next steps and a contact for follow-up.

Sam (oncall): one more practical rule: status page updates should be written in plain english first, then in parallel generate a slightly more technical note for engineering channels. The oncall-bot should produce both drafts.

Nina: action items from this thread: Rae 0 draft canned symptom lines into a support snippets file; Sam 0 wire up oncall-bot autopopulation and require a comms owner confirmation step; Liam 0 draft forbidden-phrases doc and post-incident RCA template; Nina 0 compile final templates, add curl verification examples, and open the PR to the incident playbook.

Rae (Support): I27ll aim to have canned lines mapped and PR-ready by EOD.

Sam (oncall): will implement the bot changes (or at least the PR) in the next 24h.

Nina: thanks everyone. Once PR merges we will update the incident playbook and roll the changes into the oncall-bot. Posting a reminder in #eng-oncall and #support after merge. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Template PR opened by Nina (#467). Reviewers: Sam, Rae, Liam.

Liam (Product): small closing note 0 keep templates short, single-scan, and include the "how to verify" and "who to contact" lines on every external message.

Nina: agreed. Locking brevity and verification as hard constraints. If anyone sees wording we should change before PR review, post here.
